validity.recommendation: no change; optional: note the operator-succession nuance in ResearcherNotes
validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE: well documented -- Norilsktransgaz's own history/production pages, the Gazprom Proektirovanie (VNIPIgazdobycha) engineering encyclopedia, Заполярная Правда trade press (2020), and Таймырский телеграф (2023) all independently describe the Messoyakha-Norilsk gas pipeline and its multi-line ('нитка') build-out. CLASSIFICATION: correctly a transmission trunk gas pipeline (магистральный газопровод), not a gathering/process line. SPEC: Length 263 km / Diameter 720 mm both match the Gazprom Proektirovanie encyclopedia's explicit 1969-commissioning passage naming the pipeline directly ('Газопровод Мессояха — Норильск протяженностью 263 км и диаметром 720 мм ... сдан в эксплуатацию' in 1969). DUPLICATE: no other roster PID plausibly duplicates string I -- P6683/P6684 (Pelyatka-Messoyakha) are the upstream feeder section, a distinct corridor. ATTRIBUTION CAVEAT (not scored as a concern): the recorded Operator, Norilsktransgaz JSC, was only formed in Nov 2016, decades after string I's 1967-1969 build and long after its presumed retirement (last documented as operating per a 2009 Norilskgazprom annual report per prior researcher notes); Norilsktransgaz is the correct CURRENT legal successor/asset-holder (it took over ALL of Norilskgazprom's gas-transport pipeline fixed assets in the 2016 split, per both norilsktgaz.ru and gazetazp.ru), but was never the entity that built or ran the line during 1969-2016 -- that was Norilskgazprom (and predecessor Zapolyarьegaz). This is a succession fact, not an error; no contested value proposed.

verifications.note: History timeline: 'Март 1967 года – на Мессояхской площади ... получен первый промышленный приток газа. Принято решение начать проектирование и строительство газопровода' (decision to begin design+construction of the pipeline taken March 1967); site never uses the compound name 'Мессояха-Норильск' but the whole entry is about the Messoyakha field's pipeline to the Norilsk TEC, hand-confirmed.

'В 1968 году специалисты института приступили к проектированию ... Мессояхского ГКМ и газопровода Мессояха — Норильск' (design work began 1968) and 'прокладка газопровода была осуществлена ... всего за два года' ending with 1969 commissioning -- physical construction spans ~1967/68-1969.

fills.researcher_notes: Two independent sources place the Messoyakha-Norilsk (string I) design/construction start at 1967-1968: Norilsktransgaz's own history page dates the DECISION to begin design and construction to March 1967 (right after first industrial gas flow at Messoyakha); the Gazprom Proektirovanie (VNIPIgazdobycha) engineering encyclopedia entry dates institute DESIGN work to 1968 and says physical laying took 'just two years' ending in the 1969 commissioning. GEM's recorded ConstructionYear=1967 is consistent with the design-decision date; note the one-year design-start discrepancy (1967 vs 1968) in case a future pass wants to split Construction vs a separate 'design began' data point. Both sources independently corroborate a 1967-1969 build window and the 1969 StartYear1 (see the Start [ref] fill).

verifications.note: 'Декабрь 1969 года – строительство газопровода в Заполярье в рекордно короткие сроки завершено. Первый надземный газопровод принят в эксплуатацию' -- December 1969, construction complete, first above-ground pipeline commissioned.

'В 1969 году Газопровод Мессояха — Норильск протяженностью 263 км и диаметром 720 мм ... был сдан в эксплуатацию' -- names the pipeline directly, states 1969 commissioning AND states 263 km / 720 mm, matching the recorded Length/Diameter for string I too.

fills.researcher_notes: Two independent sources (Norilsktransgaz's own history page and the Gazprom Proektirovanie/VNIPIgazdobycha engineering encyclopedia) both state the Messoyakha-Norilsk pipeline (string I) was commissioned in 1969, matching GEM's StartYear1=1969 exactly. The Gazprom encyclopedia source also explicitly names the pipeline 'Газопровод Мессояха — Норильск' and states 263 km / 720 mm diameter, matching recorded Length/Diameter for this row too (those cells already carry values on the sheet; noted here for the record though Length/Diameter [ref] were not owed units in this slice).

verifications.note: '1 ноября 2016 года – создано Акционерное общество «Норильсктрансгаз» ... приобрело право собственности на основные средства АО «Норильскгазпром», предназначенные для транспортировки газа ... по трубопроводам' -- AO Norilsktransgaz formed Nov 2016, took ownership of the gas-transport pipeline assets.

Заполярная Правда profile: 'Норильсктрансгаз ... стал полноправным владельцем всей газотранспортной системы от Пеляткинского ... ГКМ до Норильска' -- states Norilsktransgaz is sole owner/operator of the ENTIRE gas transport system from the Pelyatka field to Norilsk, i.e. including the Messoyakha-Norilsk corridor.

fills.researcher_notes: Norilsktransgaz JSC (formed Nov 2016 as a spinoff of Norilskgazprom) is confirmed by two independent sources as owner/operator of the whole Messoyakha-Norilsk gas transport corridor, string I included. CAVEAT: string I was built 1967-1969 and is recorded RETIRED, decades before Norilsktransgaz existed (est. 2016) -- the historical builder/operator (1969-2016) was Norilskgazprom (and its predecessor 'Zapolyarьegaz'), not Norilsktransgaz. Norilsktransgaz is the correct CURRENT legal successor/asset holder (per both sources, it took over ALL gas-transport pipeline fixed assets, including decommissioned ones, in the 2016 reorganization), so 'Operator = Norilsktransgaz JSC' is defensible as the present-day record-holder even for a retired line, but this is a succession attribution, not a claim Norilsktransgaz built or ran it during 1969-2016. Tier medium given this nuance; tier would be high for an operating string (see P5666-P5668).

status_reviews.researcher_notes: Two dated sources newer than the sheet's prior evidence (a 2009 Norilskgazprom annual report, per the previous researcher's note) corroborate string I remains out of service: (1) Заполярная Правда 2020 profile names ongoing maintenance/upgrade programs as covering only 'нитках 2, 3, 4' (lines 2, 3, 4) -- string I is conspicuously absent from the active-line maintenance list; (2) Norilsktransgaz's own current production page (site copyright 2023) describes the Messoyakha-Norilsk section as 'трёхниточного исполнения' (three-line design), i.e. three currently-active lines, consistent with 4 built historically and 1 (string I) retired. No source found announcing reactivation. Searched: norilsktgaz.ru (history + production pages), Nornickel investor/annual-report pages (ar2022.nornickel.com JS shell, no static text reachable), ttelegraf.ru archive, gazetazp.ru. CONFIRM retired, evidence_date ~2023 (site's stated copyright/'as of' year; no more precise date found for a negative/absence claim).

summary: String I confirmed (caveat: Operator=Norilsktransgaz JSC is the post-2016 legal successor, not the 1969-era builder/operator); Construction/Start/Operator refs added, retired status confirmed via 2020/2023 sources naming only lines 2-4 as currently active.
